$comment: Open-gaps register (plan J-7). Reviewed, curated entries; the generator appends entries derived from the matrix (untested mechanisms, per-polarity gaps, unsupported cells). Every entry needs an owner ("unassigned" when none is named) and a status: open | in-progress | accepted-limitation.

gaps.title: ML-DSA hedged signing with a caller-supplied rnd is not reachable through PKCS #11
gaps.detail: CK_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT carries hedgeVariant and context only; there is no parameter for an explicit rnd, so NIST hedged sigGen expected signatures cannot be reproduced on either engine. Shown in the workbench as an explicit skip (mldsa-skip-hedged-rnd-*) and here as unsupported rows.

gaps.title: HashML-DSA with SHA2-512/224 or SHA2-512/256 has no PKCS #11 mechanism
gaps.detail: PKCS #11 v3.2 §6.67.7 defines no CKM_HASH_ML_DSA_<hash> for these two hashes; the NIST sigVer groups for them are listed as notExecuted in mldsa_sigver_test.json.

gaps.title: ML-DSA internal interface (raw M′) is not expressible through PKCS #11
gaps.detail: No PKCS #11 v3.2 mechanism exposes Sign_internal/Verify_internal on a caller-supplied M′; the NIST internal-interface groups without external mu are listed as notExecuted.

gaps.title: KMAC256 vector case quarantined
gaps.detail: kmac_test.json tg0/tc0: the expected MAC does not match the cited NIST KMAC Sample #4 (63 bytes for a 512-bit macLen). Quarantined in the manifest; it cannot count as evidence, so CKM_KMAC_256 has no registered test.

gaps.title: 106 C++/Rust C_GetMechanismInfo disagreements
gaps.detail: Triaged 2026-09-25 against pqctoday-hsm @ a22e6ca0 (post PRs #255/#257-260): 106 mechanisms differ across 144 (mechanism, field) pairs. Classified against docs/pkcs11-mechanism-ledger.json and tests/differential/exceptions.json: ~24 now resolved by E17's HMAC min-key-size fix; ~42 deliberate/documented (named key-size-range or capability exceptions, e.g. LEGAL-MECHANISM-INFO-KEY-SIZE-RANGES, LEGAL-RSA-X509-CAPABILITY-DIFFERENCE); ~58 genuine unresolved advertisement bugs; ~20 not confidently classifiable (PKCS#11 v3.2 is silent and the repo's own exceptions have never individually adjudicated them - needs a human PKCS#11 SME opinion, not another automated pass). Top actionable item: 52 of the 58 bugs share one root cause - Rust's C_MessageSignInit already delegates to C_SignInit and works for RSA-PKCS-sign (20), CKM_HASH_ML_DSA* (11), CKM_HASH_SLH_DSA* (11) and CKM_ECDSA* (10), but the mechanism_info arms in rust/src/ffi.rs (~1481, ~1628-1648, ~1201) were never updated to advertise CKF_MESSAGE_SIGN|CKF_MESSAGE_VERIFY, unlike cpp's already-set precedent (SoftHSM_slots.cpp, 'audit mech G2'). Remaining 6: CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE/_COFACTOR_DERIVE missing CKF_EC_COMMOM (cpp, ~1210); CKM_X25519/CKM_X448 report 0/0 key-size range instead of 255/448 (cpp, ~1225); CKM_BIP32_MASTER/CHILD_DERIVE report 0/0 instead of 32/32 (cpp, vendor-only, low priority). None of this is fixed yet - awaiting a decision on whether to open a follow-up PR.

gaps.title: 9 mechanisms advertised by Rust only
gaps.detail: CKM_RIPEMD160, CKM_RIPEMD160_HMAC, CKM_RIPEMD160_HMAC_GENERAL, CKM_PQCTODAY_FRODOKEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_PQCTODAY_FRODOKEM_ENCAPSULATE, CKM_KECCAK_256, CKM_EC_MONTGOMERY_KEY_DERIVE, and — new as of the P3 combined rebuild (2026-09-25, hsm a22e6ca0, E19) — CKM_HPKE_KEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN and CKM_HPKE (advertise==dispatch closed what dispatched-not-advertised previously hid; these two are now visible, untested, Rust-only cells, waived pending-review as baseline-CKM_HPKE_KEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN / baseline-CKM_HPKE) are listed by the Rust engine only; their C++ cells are unsupported.

gaps.title: Rust dispatches CKM_BIP32_*_LEGACY without advertising them; C++ still dispatches RIPEMD160* only under its own non-advertised build flag
gaps.detail: PARTIALLY CLOSED 2026-09-25 (P3 combined rebuild, hsm a22e6ca0, E19): CKM_HPKE / CKM_HPKE_KEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN are fixed — Rust now advertises what it dispatches (advertise==dispatch), confirmed via the regenerated mechanism-dispatch-report (0x80000013/0x80000014 no longer in Rust's dispatchedMinusAdvertised list; they moved to rust-only-mechanisms as real, advertised, untested cells). Still open: the dispatch report still lists Rust CKM_BIP32_MASTER_DERIVE_LEGACY / CKM_BIP32_CHILD_DERIVE_LEGACY as dispatched-not-advertised (unchanged by any of the 6 PRs), and C++'s 3 RIPEMD160 mechanisms remain dispatched only under `WITH_RIPEMD160` while un-advertised in the same build (their dispatch site now correctly carries the same `[only if defined(WITH_RIPEMD160)]` guard as their advertisement, closing the SOURCE-level inconsistency E19 targeted for C++ — but the static dispatch report cannot see which build flag ships, so the finding itself stays open).

gaps.title: Native targets not run
gaps.detail: macOS, Linux x86-64 and Linux Arm64 native builds have not executed these registered tests; the native artifact column is "not run" and never counts as pass.

gaps.title: Hardware targets not run
gaps.detail: i.MX 95 and KV260 have not executed these registered tests; no frozen evidence bundle exists. The hardware artifact column is "not run" and never counts as pass.

gaps.title: Run results recorded only for the workbench and katRunner, on the wasm engines, in Node
gaps.detail: src/data/validation/run-results/ holds one recorded run of useAcvpSuite (all categories, both engines) and one of every registered katRunner case (both engines asserted, the Rust engine recorded — the engine the KAT surfaces use), executed in Node against the shipped .wasm bytes. The mechanism probes and the conformance cases have no recorded results, so their cells are never reported as passed. A browser-host run and a signed evidence bundle (H-1, H-7) do not exist yet.

gaps.title: Native 976/815-check engine suites not in the evidence pipeline
gaps.detail: The larger native C++/Rust conformance suites are not imported, so none of their cases appear in this matrix.

gaps.title: PKCS #11 API-behavior matrix not built
gaps.detail: OASIS Tier A cases and the generated Tier B profile-condition probes that exercise sessions, login, objects and attributes are registered (testRegistry oasis.api-only, profile.api-only) but are outside this algorithm × operation matrix.

gaps.title: SLH-DSA NIST sigGen cases registered but not executed
gaps.detail: slhdsa_ctx_test.json /sigGen cases are in the manifest for identity but no runner executes them (deterministic sigGen byte-match), so SLH-DSA sign has round-trip evidence only.

gaps.title: Supported ACVP test types (AFT/MCT/LDT/VAL) not declared per algorithm
gaps.detail: The capability map declares parameter sets, variants and boundaries, but not which ACVP test types each capability should support; the matrix lists only the test types its registered NIST cases exercise.

gaps.title: Some test surfaces are not in the test registry
gaps.detail: Not registered: Learn-module demos outside KatValidationPanel (the SUCI flow's own step-by-step tool among them) and the *.local.test.ts engine suites that are not run-results recorders. Their evidence does not appear in this matrix. (The katRunner suci-profile-b chain is registered since 2026-09-24: steps 3-7 against TS 33.501 Annex C.4.4.1.)

gaps.title: ECDSA P-521 NIST sample failed on C++ — hub CKA_EC_POINT encoding (fixed hub-side)
gaps.detail: Root cause (triage 2026-09-24): hsm_importECPublicKey wrote the DER OCTET STRING length of the 133-byte P-521 point as the single byte 0x85, which DER reads as '5 length octets follow'; the C++ engine parsed a garbage CKA_EC_POINT and rejected the NIST ACVP-Server ECDSA-SigVer-FIPS186-5 sample (workbench §33), while Rust passed because it reads the raw CKA_VALUE copy. Hub adapter bug, not an engine defect. Fixed by the X.690 long-form length (softhsm/helpers derOctetString); the re-recorded run shows the case passing on both engines. Kept on record until the release freeze re-captures evidence on the browser host.

gaps.title: SUCI key-injection helper is rejected by the C++ engine
gaps.detail: hsm_injectTestKey unwraps the raw EC scalar with C_UnwrapKeyAuthenticated using a template that carries CKA_EC_PARAMS; the C++ engine rejects it with CKR_ATTRIBUTE_READ_ONLY (the same unwrap without CKA_EC_PARAMS succeeds). katRunner suci-profile-b steps 1-2 (import only, not registered) therefore error on C++; steps 3-7 import with C_CreateObject and pass on both engines. The KAT surfaces run the Rust engine. Hub helper limitation.

gaps.title: PKCS #11 v3.2 gives no single key-handle / key-type code for C_DecapsulateKey — not probed
gaps.detail: §5.18.9 lists CKR_UNWRAPPING_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID and CKR_UNWRAPPING_KEY_TYPE_INCONSISTENT (not CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID / CKR_KEY_TYPE_INCONSISTENT), while §5.1.6 says the UNWRAPPING_* codes "can only be returned by C_UnwrapKey". With no single specified value there is no key-handle or key-type probe for C_DecapsulateKey (the engines differ: C++ returns CKR_UNWRAPPING_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID for handle 0, Rust CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID). Likewise C_WrapKey, C_UnwrapKey, C_DeriveKey and C_EncapsulateKey require the usage attribute but do not list CKR_KEY_FUNCTION_NOT_PERMITTED, so no key-usage probe exists for them. Specification ambiguity, not an engine defect. Recorded by the G-8 error-path probes (errorPathCatalog.ts / errorPathProbes.ts) in run-results/wasm-node-errorPathProbes.json; the rows stay failing — the assertion is the PKCS #11 v3.2 value and is not loosened.

gaps.title: Classical NIST reference samples cover only what the pinned upstream samples register
gaps.detail: The pinned ACVP-Server@975de31e samples bound what WS-E can claim: ACVP-AES-GCM-1.0 registers AES-128 only (IV 96/120, tag 128/32, payload/AAD 0/120 bits) — AES-192/256-GCM, 64-bit tags and other lengths have no NIST case; HMAC 2.0 registers macLen 80..160 bits — no full-length (untruncated) tag, so CKM_<hash>_HMAC (non-general) has no NIST case; EDDSA-SigVer-1.0 carries no context string (contexts are exercised only through the EDDSA-SigGen-1.0 byte-match cases of eddsa_siggen_acvp_test); ECDSA SHA2-512/256 and SHAKE groups have no PKCS#11 v3.2 CKM_ECDSA_<hash> mechanism (skip rows). Checked again 2026-09-25 (GitHub API, gap-closure P5): 975de31e (2026-08-12, "RELEASE/v1.1.0.43 including hotfix patches") is still the head of usnistgov/ACVP-Server master and the only other branch (jbrock24-patch-1, 2024) changes the README only, so no newer upstream commit carries AES-192/256-GCM or full-length HMAC tag samples; the scope gap stays.

gaps.title: Classical families still without NIST ACVP-Server cases after WS-E and gap-closure P5
gaps.detail: Closed by gap-closure P5 (2026-09-25): HKDF (hkdf_acvp_test, KDA-HKDF-Sp800-56Cr2), SP 800-108 KBKDF (kbkdf_acvp_test, KDF 1.0 counter / feedback / double pipeline), ECDSA/EdDSA KeyVer (ecdsa_/eddsa_keyver_acvp_test, the key is used: sign with d, verify with the point), ECDSA SigGen verify-back (functional round-trip + independent oracle; NIST r, s are not reproducible because C_Sign draws its own nonce), EdDSA SigGen byte-match, the alternate-version SHA-2 MCT and full 100-iteration MCTs for SHA-2/SHA-3 and AES-CBC (sha_mct_full_test, aescbc_mct_full_test). Still open: ANSI X9.63 KDF on a caller-supplied Z — not expressible through PKCS #11 (declaredUnreachable x963-kdf-caller-z, gap x963-kdf-caller-z-no-mechanism); SHA LDT (1 GiB expanded message); HKDF multi-expansion groups; KBKDF with CMAC-TDES, HMAC-SHA2-512/224, /256 or bit-oriented output lengths; ECDSA/EdDSA KeyGen and deterministic ECDSA SigGen (no PKCS #11 input for the random / RFC 6979 nonce). The older HKDF/PBKDF2/X9.63/KBKDF workbench rows keep their published-standard / oracle / round-trip labels.

gaps.title: ANSI X9.63 KDF on a caller-supplied shared secret has no PKCS #11 mechanism
gaps.detail: PKCS #11 v3.2 defines the X9.63 KDF only as the CK_EC_KDF_TYPE of CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE and related ECDH mechanisms (§6.3.16), applied to the shared secret the token derives from its own key pair; no mechanism accepts a caller-supplied Z, so the NIST kdf-components-ansix9.63-1.0 cases (Z, sharedInfo -> keyData) cannot be executed. Shown as the workbench skip row x963-kdf-unsupported and the capability-map declaredUnreachable row x963-kdf-caller-z. The KDF itself is exercised inside ECDH derivation (section 25, round-trip only).

gaps.title: C++: SP 800-108 KDFs ignore where the caller places the counter in the PRF input
gaps.detail: With the PKCS #11 v3.2 §6.42 data-parameter layout the NIST KDF 1.0 cases require, the C++ engine derives the wrong key whenever the counter is not in its fixed position: counter mode with the ITERATION_VARIABLE after or in the middle of the fixed data, and feedback / double-pipeline with a COUNTER before the chaining value or after the fixed data (kbkdf_acvp_test, 12 rows per run: HMAC-SHA2-256 and CMAC-AES128). 'Before fixed data' (and no counter) layouts byte-match NIST for every PRF. The engine appears to place the counter first (counter mode) or right after K(i-1)/A(i) (feedback / double pipeline) regardless of the CK_PRF_DATA_PARAM order. Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

gaps.title: Rust: feedback and double-pipeline KBKDF reject the mandatory ITERATION_VARIABLE data parameter
gaps.detail: PKCS #11 v3.2 §6.42.4/§6.42.5 make CK_SP800_108_ITERATION_VARIABLE mandatory in feedback and double-pipeline mode (pValue NULL, ulValueLen 0; §6.42.2). The Rust engine returns CKR_MECHANISM_PARAM_INVALID for every such layout, so all 38 feedback / double-pipeline NIST KDF 1.0 rows fail. Probed 2026-09-25: without the ITERATION_VARIABLE entry the engine accepts the parameters and reproduces NIST except where the counter precedes the chaining value. Counter mode (ITERATION_VARIABLE with a counter format) is correct in every location. The hub keeps the specification layout; the existing sections 27/29 call the feedback mechanism without the ITERATION_VARIABLE. Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

gaps.title: C++: invalid ECDSA / EdDSA public points are imported and used without validation
gaps.detail: The NIST keyVer cases with a point not on the curve or a coordinate out of range (ecdsa_keyver_acvp_test P-256/384/521, eddsa_keyver_acvp_test Ed25519/Ed448: 10 points) are accepted by C_CreateObject and C_VerifyInit, and C_Verify then returns CKR_SIGNATURE_INVALID as for any wrong signature — no FIPS 186-5 / SP 800-56A public-key validation happens on import or use (PKCS #11 v3.2 §4.1.1 would return CKR_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID at creation). Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

gaps.title: Rust: invalid public points are refused only at C_Verify, with a code C_Verify does not list
gaps.detail: The Rust engine imports the 10 invalid NIST keyVer points (C_CreateObject CKR_OK) and accepts C_VerifyInit, then C_Verify returns CKR_KEY_TYPE_INCONSISTENT — not among the §5.15.2 C_Verify return values. The keyVer rows pass (the point is refused with a key error), but validation belongs at C_CreateObject (§4.1.1 CKR_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID) or C_VerifyInit.

gaps.title: Rust: Ed25519ph / Ed448ph signing ignores the CK_EDDSA_PARAMS context
gaps.detail: C_Sign(CKM_EDDSA, phFlag = true, non-empty context) on the Rust engine produces the Ed25519ph / Ed448ph signature for an EMPTY context: all 8 preHash NIST EDDSA-SigGen-1.0 cases (contexts 96–248 bytes) differ from NIST, and @noble/curves ed25519ph verifies the Rust output without the context and rejects it with it. Pure Ed25519 / Ed448 with contexts byte-match. The C++ engine matches all 16 cases. Engine defect — not patched in the hub.
